name: CyberPower UPS
author: kamil
description: CyberPower UPS status in the bar: battery, runtime, load and mains voltage, read straight off the USB HID device, with pwrstat and NUT fallbacks and an optional event history.

barWidget.description: Shows charge, runtime and power state of a CyberPower USB UPS. Click for details and self-test or alarm controls.

schema.label: Data source
schema.description: Auto tries a direct USB read first, then pwrstat, then NUT. Simulate shows sample data with no UPS attached. The key is called backend and not source on purpose: a bar entry with a setting called source is read as a custom QML module by the shell, and the widget then renders as nothing.

schema.label: NUT UPS name
schema.description: Required by the NUT backend. Leave empty to use the first UPS upsc lists.

schema.label: Refresh interval (seconds)
schema.description: How often to poll the UPS. Direct USB reads are cheap; 15-30 seconds is plenty.

schema.label: Show battery percentage
schema.description: Print the charge beside the icon. Off leaves just the icon.

schema.label: Icon style
schema.description: Auto uses a battery glyph that tracks charge; Power always uses a power/battery-carrying glyph.

schema.label: Low battery warning (%)
schema.description: Tint the icon when charge drops to or below this while on battery.

schema.label: Critical battery (%)
schema.description: Use the urgent color at or below this charge.

schema.label: Show self-test controls
schema.description: Show the Self-test and Abort buttons in the popup. Turn off if the UPS's test beeps are unwelcome; the CLI can still run tests on demand.

schema.label: Shut down at battery capacity (%)
schema.description: PowerPanel calls this Consume Battery Capacity: the machine powers itself off when the charge falls to this percentage. 0 leaves that half of the rule off.

schema.label: Shut down after running on battery (minutes)
schema.description: PowerPanel calls this Preserve Battery Power: the machine powers itself off once the UPS has run on battery for this many minutes, whichever of the three runtime rules comes first. 0 leaves that half of the rule off.

schema.label: Shut down at remaining runtime (minutes)
schema.description: PowerPanel's "Shutdown this computer when remaining battery runtime is only xxxx minutes": the machine powers itself off when the UPS estimates this little runtime remains. Unlike a capacity limit it accounts for the load, so it is the safer rule on a UPS whose firmware cuts the output on its own timer. 0 leaves that half of the rule off.

schema.label: Warning countdown before shutdown (seconds)
schema.description: How long the widget counts down, with a notification and a Cancel button, before it powers the machine off. The UPS keeps supplying power during the countdown.

schema.label: Write a debug trace
schema.description: Record every device read and write to ~/.local/state/cyberpower-ups/debug.log. Leave off for normal use; turn on when reporting a problem.
